pairs.question: Cuius tandem ego rei praeter opinionem, quae sua cuique coniectanti esse potest, auctor sim?
pairs.answer: Simile ueri est aut interuallis bellorum, sicut nunc in dilectibus fit Romanis, alia atque alia subole iuniorum ad bella instauranda totiens usos esse aut non ex iisdem semper populis exercitus scriptos, quamquam eadem semper gens bellum intulerit, aut innumerabilem multitudinem liberorum capitum in eis fuisse locis quae nunc uix seminario exiguo militum relicto seruitia Romana ab solitudine uindicant.
pairs.derivation: Livy interrupts the narrative (the digression marked off by dashes in section 12) to pose, and then answer, his own question about how the repeatedly-defeated Volsci and Aequi kept supplying soldiers. The question span is his direct self-posed interrogative 'cuius tandem ego rei... auctor sim?' (first word capitalized, terminal '?' kept). The preceding clause 'unde totiens uictis Volscis et Aequis suffecerint milites' states the puzzle in indirect discourse with framing ('non dubito... legentibus illud quoque succursurum, quod mihi percensenti... miraculo fuit unde...'), so it is narration of the question and is dropped rather than stitched in. The answer begins at 'simile ueri est...', his actual conjecture, and is cut at the first full stop after 'uindicant' (the next sentence 'ingens certe, quod inter omnes auctores conueniat...' turns to the size of the Volscian army, a separate point). No interior ellipsis; all words verbatim and in source order, only the first letter capitalized.
